column2: Soundview Academy for Culture and Scholarship
column6: Marissa Molina, Danielle Mastrion, Pelumi Ayeni
column13: Soundview Academy in the Bronx got even more murals in 2025. "Dream Big" was created by Marissa Molina, Danielle Mastrion, and Pelumi Ayeni. Small dreams lead to small lives. Big dreams lead to big lives. The artists painted students reaching for stars, planets, and galaxies. The mural at 1160 Colgate Avenue is a dare. Do not dream about getting a new backpack. Dream about becoming an astronaut. When you look at it, you are seeing children given permission to think huge.

column2: Soundview Academy for Culture and Scholarship
column6: Marissa Molina, Danielle Mastrion, Pelumi Ayeni
column13: Embrace Diversity was another Soundview Academy mural in 2025, created by Marissa Molina, Danielle Mastrion, and Pelumi Ayeni. Many schools talk about diversity. This school painted it. The artists worked with students to draw faces of every skin tone, abilities of every kind, and families of every shape. The mural at 1160 Colgate Avenue is a mirror and a window. When you look at it, you see yourself, and you see someone not like you. That is the point. Embrace both.

column6: Marissa Molina, Raisa Oliveira Da Silva
column13: PS 86Q in Jamaica, Queens, also got "Serenity" in 2025, created by Marissa Molina and Raisa Oliveira Da Silva. School is stressful. Life is loud. The artists painted quiet scenes. A still lake. A sleeping cat. A child reading alone in a sunny window. The mural at 87-41 80th Street is a breathing exercise. When you look at it, your shoulders drop. Your heart slows. That is the gift of "Serenity." A moment of peace in a chaotic day.

column6: Marissa Molina, Raisa Oliveira Da Silva
column13: Student Medicine was another PS 86Q mural in 2025, created by Marissa Molina and Raisa Oliveira Da Silva. Not just cough syrup and bandages. Friendship, laughter, art, and rest. The artists asked students what medicine they needed. The answers became the mural. A hug. A good grade. A game of tag. The mural at 87-41 80th Street is a prescription written by children. When you look at it, you are seeing a different kind of pharmacy. One that costs nothing but works wonders.

column1: PS 60Q: Make Each Day Your Masterpiece
column6: Marissa Molina, Raissa Oliveira Da Silva
column13: PS 60Q in Woodhaven, Queens, got a mural in 2025 called "Make Each Day Your Masterpiece," created by Marissa Molina and Raissa Oliveira Da Silva. You do not need to paint a masterpiece every day. You need to try. The artists painted students holding paintbrushes, but the canvases were their days. A Monday. A Tuesday. A rainy Wednesday. The mural at 55 Merrill Avenue is a motto for living. Not perfection. Intention. When you look at it, you are seeing permission to make today beautiful, even if yesterday was not.

column6: Marissa Molina, WEN COD, Wale Ayeni, Amber Smalls, Lola Lovenotes, Loreto
column13: RTG West at P.S. 126 in Highbridge, Bronx, got a mural in 2025 called "Peacemakers Play," created by Marissa Molina, WEN COD, Wale Ayeni, Amber Smalls, Lola Lovenotes, and Loreto. Peace is not passive. It takes work. The artists painted children playing games that require cooperation. Building blocks. Team sports. Sharing toys. The mural at 80 Catherine Street is a workshop. When you look at it, you are seeing the skills of peace taught through play. That is how children learn best.

column1: Park East HS: Bloom in Time
column13: Park East High School in El Barrio, Manhattan, got a mural in 2025 called "Bloom in Time," created by artist May Bukowski. Flowers do not bloom overnight. Neither do students. Bukowski painted flowers at different stages. Seeds, sprouts, buds, and full blooms. The mural at 230 East 105th Street is a reassurance for every student who feels behind. You will bloom. In time. When you look at it, you are seeing a reminder that growth cannot be rushed. But it will come.

column1: Chelsea Preparatory Academy: Your Mind is a Garden
column13: Chelsea Preparatory Academy in Manhattan got a mural in 2025 called "Your Mind is a Garden," created by May Bukowski and Mirian Cruz. A garden needs watering, weeding, and sunlight. So does a mind. The artists painted gardens with different plants representing different thoughts. Kindness as sunflowers. Curiosity as vines. Fear as weeds to be pulled. The mural at 103 West 27th Street is a mental health lesson. When you look at it, you are learning to garden your own brain. Plant good seeds. Pull the bad ones.

PS/MS 104K in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, got a mural in 2025 called "Mark of Excellence," created by artist Michael "Kaves" McCleer. Excellence is not an accident. It is a mark you leave. Kaves painted students leaving their marks on the world. A published book. A patented invention. A healed patient. The mural at 9115 5th Avenue is a challenge. What mark will you leave? When you look at it, you are seeing a school that expects greatness. Not for fame. For legacy.

IS 220K in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, got a mural in 2025 called "Time Capsule," created by artist Michela Muserra as part of a CPC Beacon project. What would you put in a time capsule for the future? Muserra asked students that question. They drew photographs, letters, and small toys. The mural at 4812 9th Avenue became the capsule itself. When you look at it, you are seeing what this generation wants the future to know about them. We were here. We loved. We hoped.

column6: Michela Muserra, Wale Ayeni, Ralph DeMaio, Motoko Otsuki, Melissa Schainker
column13: MS 61K in Prospect Lefferts Gardens, Brooklyn, got a mural in 2025 called "We Write the Future," created by Michela Muserra, Wale Ayeni, Ralph DeMaio, Motoko Otsuki, and Melissa Schainker. The future is not something that happens to you. You write it. The artists painted students holding pens, typing on laptops, and chiseling words into stone. The mural at 400 Empire Boulevard is a declaration of power. When you look at it, you are seeing young authors. Their medium is not paper. It is time itself.

column6: Nico Collazo, May Bukowski, Christine DiPasquale, Motoko Otsuki
column10: E 10th St & Ave D, New York, NY 10009
column13: The Art of Healing series in Dry Dock Park on the Lower East Side included "Breathe LES" in 2025, created by Nico Collazo, May Bukowski, Christine DiPasquale, and Motoko Otsuki. The Lower East Side is busy, loud, and fast. Breathing helps. The artists painted deep breaths as colorful waves, expanding lungs, and calm faces. The mural at East 10th Street and Avenue D is a yoga class in paint. When you look at it, you are being invited to stop. Just for a moment. And breathe.

column6: Nico Collazo, May Bukowski, Christine DiPasquale, Motoko Otsuki
column10: E 10th St & Ave D, New York, NY 10009
column13: Love Soul was another Art of Healing mural in Dry Dock Park in 2025. Before you can love anyone else, you have to love your own soul. The artists painted portraits of people looking in mirrors and seeing someone worthy of love. The mural at East 10th Street and Avenue D is a mirror for everyone who passes. When you look at it, you are supposed to see yourself. And love what you see.

column1: Bronx Arts Middle School: Bronx Express
column13: Bronx Arts Middle School in Soundview got a mural in 2025 called "Bronx Express," created by Nico Collazo and Ralph Demaio. The Bronx is always moving. Trains, buses, cars, and feet. The artists painted a subway train made of musical instruments, book covers, and paintbrushes. The mural at 1440 Story Avenue is a portrait of the Bronx as a cultural express. When you look at it, you are seeing art, music, and literature rushing through the borough like a train. Do not miss your stop.

The Amazin' Mets Foundation partnered with Thrive Collective in 2025 to create "Amazin' Family" at Citi Field in Queens, created by artist Peach Tao. The Mets are not just a team. They are a family. Tao painted Mets fans of all ages, races, and backgrounds, united in their blue and orange. The mural at 41 Seaver Way is a stadium within a stadium. When you look at it, you are seeing the seventh inning stretch extended into a permanent celebration. L.G.M. Let's Go Mets.

column1: PS 76 & SAFE in Harlem: Dream On
column13: PS 76 in Harlem got a mural in 2025 called "Dream On," created by Peach Tao and Andrea Amanda with help from student Anaiyah Smith. Dreams do not always come true on schedule. You have to dream on. The artists painted children sleeping, but their dreams floated above them as colorful balloons. The mural at 220 West 121st Street is a lullaby and a pep talk. When you look at it, you are being told not to give up on your dreams. Even if they take longer than you hoped. Dream on.

PS 91X in Highbridge, Bronx, got a mural in 2025 called "Spread Your Wings," created by Peach Tao and Chey Nelson. Every child will eventually leave home. The question is whether they will be ready. The artists painted birds taking flight for the first time, nervous but excited. The mural at 2220 Aqueduct Avenue is a parenting lesson in paint. When you look at it, you are seeing the moment before the leap. The flutter. The fear. The freedom. Spread your wings.

column2: P.S 212 The Lady Deborah Moody School
column13: P.S. 212 The Lady Deborah Moody School in Gravesend, Brooklyn, celebrated 100 years in 2025 with a mural called "100 Years of Excellence," created by artist Pelumi Ayeni. A century of teaching children is worth celebrating. Ayeni painted images from each decade. Old photographs, vintage uniforms, and century old hallways next to modern classrooms. The mural at 87 Bay 49th Street is a time machine. When you look at it, you are seeing a hundred years of first days of school, of chalk dust, of young minds opening. That is excellence.

column1: SVA Mural Makeover: Larger than Life
column2: Soundview Academy for Culture and Scholarship
column13: Soundview Academy's mural makeover continued with "Larger than Life," created by Pelumi Ayeni in 2025. Students are often made to feel small. This mural makes them feel large. Ayeni painted students as giants, towering over buildings and trees. The mural at 1160 Colgate Avenue is a perspective shift. When you look at it, you are seeing children the way they deserve to see themselves. Not as problems to be solved. As forces to be reckoned with. Larger than life.

column1: IS 131 Albert Einstein School: Beauty and Strength
column13: IS 131 Albert Einstein School in Soundview, Bronx, got a series of murals in 2025 created by Pelumi Ayeni and Wale Ayeni. The first was "Beauty and Strength." Girls are told to be beautiful. Boys are told to be strong. This mural says everyone can be both. The artists painted figures who are soft and hard, gentle and powerful, beautiful and strong. The mural at 1000 Tell Avenue is a refusal of false choices. When you look at it, you are seeing wholeness. You do not have to pick one.

Galaxy was another IS 131 mural in 2025. A galaxy has billions of stars and planets. So does a child's future. The artists painted students as astronauts floating through space, reaching for distant stars. The mural at 1000 Tell Avenue is a telescope. When you look at it, you are seeing futures that have not been invented yet. That is the point. No one can predict what these students will become. The galaxy is wide open.

column1: IS 131 Albert Einstein School: Knowledge is Power
column13: Knowledge is Power was painted at IS 131 in 2025. Money gives power. Birth gives power. But knowledge gives power to anyone who seeks it. The artists painted books as superhero capes, light bulbs as crowns, and libraries as castles. The mural at 1000 Tell Avenue is a motivational poster for the information age. When you look at it, you are being reminded that no one can ever take away what you learn. That is real power.

column1: IS 131 Albert Einstein School: The Arts
column13: The Arts was another IS 131 mural in 2025. The arts are always on the chopping block when budgets get tight. This mural defends them. The artists painted musicians, dancers, actors, and painters, all in vibrant motion. The mural at 1000 Tell Avenue is a protest and a celebration. When you look at it, you are seeing why the arts matter. Not as an extra. As an essential.

column1: IS 131 Albert Einstein School: The Beat of 131
column13: The Beat of 131 was the final IS 131 mural in 2025. Every school has a heartbeat. The artists asked students what their school's beat sounded like. Drums in the band room. Sneakers in the gym. Laughter in the cafeteria. The mural at 1000 Tell Avenue is a soundtrack in paint. When you look at it, you can almost hear it. The beat of 131. It keeps going, year after year, student after student.

column1: PS 101K: "Where Will Your Wings Take You?"
column13: PS 101 The Verrazano in Gravesend, Brooklyn, got four murals in 2025 created by Pelumi Ayeni and Wale Ayeni. The first was "Where Will Your Wings Take You?" Everyone has wings. The question is where you choose to fly. The artists painted winged students flying over beaches, mountains, cities, and farms. The mural at 2360 Benson Avenue is a travel brochure for the imagination. When you look at it, you are being asked that question. Where will your wings take you? Answer honestly. Then go.

You are Welcome was the second PS 101 mural in 2025. Many students in Gravesend are immigrants or children of immigrants. "You are welcome" is not just polite. It is necessary. The artists painted the phrase in multiple languages alongside open doors and smiling faces. The mural at 2360 Benson Avenue is a greeting. When you look at it, you are being welcomed. No matter where you were born. No matter what language you speak. You belong here.

column1: PS 101K: Just the Way You Are
column13: You are Welcome was the second PS 101 mural in 2025. Many students in Gravesend are immigrants or children of immigrants. "You are welcome" is not just polite. It is necessary. The artists painted the phrase in multiple languages alongside open doors and smiling faces. The mural at 2360 Benson Avenue is a greeting. When you look at it, you are being welcomed. No matter where you were born. No matter what language you speak. You belong here.

The artists painted the phrase in multiple languages alongside open doors and smiling faces. The mural at 2360 Benson Avenue is a greeting. When you look at it, you are being welcomed. No matter where you were born. No matter what language you speak. You belong here.

column1: AACC Bronx Museum 2024: Peace, Love & Happiness
column13: The Bronx Museum of Art hosted an AACC project in 2024 called "Peace, Love & Happiness," created by artist Pips. Three words that sound simple but are hard to live by. Pips painted them in bright colors, surrounded by flowers, hearts, and smiling faces. The mural at 1040 Grand Concourse is a wish. When you look at it, you are seeing what the artist hopes for every person who walks into the museum. Peace. Love. Happiness. It is not a bad prayer.

PS 171Q in Astoria, Queens, got a massive series of murals in 2025. "FUNdamentals, Part 2" included a mural called "Gratitude," created by Plushie and Ralph Demaio. In a world that teaches children to want more, gratitude teaches them to see what they already have. The artists painted hands folded in thanks, families eating together, and children hugging grandparents. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a practice. When you look at it, you are being reminded to say thank you. For the small things. For the big things. For everything.

Compassion was another "FUNdamentals, Part 2" mural at PS 171Q in 2025. To have compassion is to feel someone else's pain. The artists painted people helping people up, crying together, and sitting in silence with those who are hurting. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a lesson in humanity. When you look at it, you are being taught that compassion is not pity. It is presence. Showing up is enough.

Trust was painted at PS 171Q in 2025. Trust is built slowly and destroyed quickly. The artists painted handshakes, pinky promises, and children trusting their friends to catch them. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a contract. When you look at it, you are seeing what trust looks like. It looks like showing up on time. Keeping your word. Being there.

Perseverance joined the PS 171Q series in 2025. Perseverance is the most important quality for success, more than talent or luck. The artists painted students climbing mountains, running races, and trying again after falling. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a fitness class for the will. When you look at it, you are seeing the beauty of getting back up. That is perseverance.

Eagles was another "FUNdamentals, Part 2" mural at PS 171Q in 2025. The eagle represents vision, strength, and freedom. The artists painted eagles soaring over Astoria, wings wide, eyes sharp. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a team cheer. When you look at it, you are hearing the school song in your head. Eagles fly high. So will you.

Magnet was another "FUNdamentals, Part 2" mural at PS 171Q in 2025. Magnet schools attract students from across the city by offering specialized programs. The artists painted magnets pulling in ideas, books, and students from every direction. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is an advertisement and a celebration. When you look at it, you are seeing why PS 171Q is a destination. Because it attracts excellence.

FUNdamentals Part 1 at PS 171Q in 2025 included "Diversity," created by Plushie, Yvette Hidalgo, and Joshua Gabriel. Astoria is one of the most diverse neighborhoods on Earth. The artists painted faces from every continent, flags from every country, and food from every cuisine. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a census in paint. When you look at it, you are seeing the world in one schoolyard. That is not a problem to solve. That is a treasure to celebrate.

Soar was another "FUNdamentals" mural at PS 171Q in 2025. First you learn to walk. Then you learn to run. Then you soar. The artists painted students launching off diving boards, springboards, and trampolines. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a promise. When you look at it, you are seeing that the basics are just the beginning. After fundamentals comes flight.

Sharing was painted at PS 171Q in 2025. The artists painted children sharing everything. Food, toys, secrets, and dreams. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a counter narrative to a culture of hoarding. When you look at it, you are being reminded that what you share does not shrink. It multiplies. That is the magic of sharing.

Family was another "FUNdamentals" mural at PS 171Q in 2025. Before school, before friends, there is family. The artists painted families eating, laughing, arguing, and reconciling. All the mess and beauty of being related. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a family album. When you look at it, you are seeing that family is not perfect. But it is yours.

Respect was the final "FUNdamentals" mural at PS 171Q in 2025. Treat others the way you want to be treated. The artists painted scenes of listening, waiting your turn, and saying please and thank you. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is an etiquette lesson. When you look at it, you are being shown that respect is not complicated. It is small choices made over and over.

The final "FUNdamentals" mural at PS 171Q brought all the themes together. The artists created a colorful, unified design that celebrated the core values of the school. The mural at 14-14 29th Avenue is a summary of everything the students learned. Fundamentals are not just rules. They are the foundation of a good life.

column6: Raissa Oliveira Da Silva, Kenneth Tooley
column13: PS/MS 183Q in Arverne, Queens, got a mural in 2025 called "Good Things Happen Here," created by Raissa Oliveira Da Silva and Kenneth Tooley. If you believe good things can happen, you are more likely to make them happen. The artists painted sunny days, blooming flowers, and smiling children. The mural at 2-45 Beach 79th Street is an affirmation. When you look at it, you are being told that this school, this neighborhood, this moment is full of possibility. Good things happen here. Believe it.

column1: Capital Hill Boys Club: God is King
column6: Ryan Mizta, Brian Bailey, Lew the Artist
column13: The Peter Bug Shoe Repair Academy on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., got two murals in 2025 created by Ryan Mizta, Brian Bailey, and Lew the Artist. The first was "God is King." Peter Bug's academy is a community institution that has served D.C. for decades. The artists painted religious imagery, hands in prayer, and words of scripture. The mural at 1320 E Street SE is a sanctuary. When you look at it, you are seeing faith made visible. For the people of Capitol Hill, God is king. That belief sustains them.

column6: Ryan Mizta, Brian Bailey, Lew the Artist
column13: The second Peter Bug mural was "Peterbug." Peter Bug himself is a local legend, a shoe repairman who became a father figure to generations. The artists painted his portrait, his tools, and his shop. The mural at 1320 E Street SE is a biography. When you look at it, you are learning about a man who fixed more than shoes. He fixed lives. That is worth painting on a wall.

column1: Mentoring Youth for Leadership Summit: City as Playground
column13: The Mentoring Youth for Leadership Summit in Chattanooga, Tennessee, got a mural in 2025 called "City as Playground," created by Sam Wisneski. Cities are often designed for cars and commerce, not for children. Wisneski asked young people to imagine the city as a playground. They painted slides on skyscrapers, swings on street corners, and seesaws in parking lots. The mural is a blueprint for a better city. When you look at it, you are seeing what happens when you ask children what they need. They need to play. Everywhere.

The Carter Center on Staten Island got a mural in 2025 called "Nike Customs," created by artist Shawn McArthur. Nike sneakers are more than shoes. They are art, status, and identity. McArthur worked with young people to customize painted sneakers on the wall, each pair telling a different story. The mural at 453 Freedom Parkway NE in Atlanta is a fashion show. When you look at it, you are seeing self expression through footwear. Your shoes say something about you. What do you want them to say?

The Barclays Center in Brooklyn got a mural in 2025 called "History Made," created by artist Toofly for the New York Liberty. The Liberty have made history, winning championships and breaking barriers. Toofly painted players in motion, screaming fans, and the words "History Made." The mural at 620 Atlantic Avenue is a victory lap. When you look at it, you are seeing the culmination of decades of struggle for recognition. The Liberty made history. This mural makes sure no one forgets.

column1: RTG South: I Want to Grow Up
column13: RTG South at the Claremont Art Walk in the Bronx's Concourse Village got several murals in 2025 created by Toofly and Lola Lovenotes. The first was "I Want to Grow Up." Every child wants to grow up, but they do not always know what that means. The artists painted children imagining their grown up selves. Firefighters, doctors, mothers, fathers. The mural at 1195 Clay Avenue is a yearbook from the future. When you look at it, you are seeing hope in the form of a child's drawing. I want to grow up. And I want to be someone.

Peacemakers, Continued was another RTG South mural in 2025. Peace is never finished. You have to keep making it. The artists painted people resolving conflicts, shaking hands, and walking away from fights. The mural at 1195 Clay Avenue is a sequel. When you look at it, you are being reminded that peace is not a destination. It is a practice. Keep going.

Together We Shine was the final RTG South mural in 2025. One star is bright. A galaxy is brighter. The artists painted constellations made of student faces, each one a star. The mural at 1195 Clay Avenue is a group portrait. When you look at it, you are seeing the whole community. Not one hero. Many heroes. Together, they shine.

PS 354Q in Jamaica, Queens, got two murals in 2025 created by Toofly and Mirian Cruz. The first was "Let's Collaborate!" No great thing was ever done alone. The artists painted students building things together. A tower of blocks. A band playing music. A mural, of course. The mural is a reminder. When you look at it, you are being invited to work with someone else. Collaboration is not compromise. It is multiplication.

The second PS 354Q mural was "Mindfulness," created by Toofly and Mirian Cruz. Students are more stressed than ever. Mindfulness helps. The artists painted children meditating, breathing deeply, and paying attention to the present moment. The mural is a wellness class. When you look at it, you are being taught that your mind is like a muscle. You can train it to be calm. Try mindfulness.

column10: 1 San Geronimo St, San Juan, PR 00901
column13: The CPC / SOMOS Conference in San Juan, Puerto Rico, got a mural in 2025 called "Solidarity," created by Tsvetana Dondero and Gabriel Abast. Solidarity is not charity. It is standing together. The artists painted linked arms, shared resources, and communities rebuilding after disaster. The mural at 1 San Geronimo Street in San Juan is a political statement. When you look at it, you are seeing Puerto Rico's strength. Not dependency. Solidarity.

column1: Frank McCourt HS: We Are One
column13: Frank McCourt High School on Manhattan's Upper West Side got a mural in 2025 called "We Are One," created by Vanesa Álvarez Díaz and Christian Bachez. The Upper West Side is wealthy and diverse, but division is always a threat. The artists painted students of all backgrounds with their hands over their hearts. The mural at 145 West 84th Street is a pledge. When you look at it, you are hearing the words "We Are One" spoken in many languages. That is the only way forward.

FDR High School in Mapleton, Brooklyn, got two more murals in 2025. "Data Science" was created by Vince Ballantine and Yasmine Rodriguez. Data science is one of the fastest growing fields. The artists painted graphs, charts, and students analyzing information. The mural at 5800 20th Avenue is a career fair. When you look at it, you are seeing that math is not just homework. Math is a career. Data science is the future.

Robotics was the second FDR High School mural in 2025. Robots are not coming. They are here. The artists painted students building robots, programming computers, and competing in robotics competitions. The mural at 5800 20th Avenue is a workshop. When you look at it, you are seeing that the students of FDR are not afraid of robots. They are building them. That is the difference between being replaced and being irreplaceable.

column2: Hillcrest High School: The Power to Change
column13: 160-05 Highland Ave, Jamaica, NY 11432
column16: Hillcrest High School in Jamaica, Queens, got a mural in 2025 called "The Power to Change," created by Will DeNatale and Yasmine Rodriguez. You have the power to change. Your life. Your community. Your world. The artists painted superheroes, but the faces were students. The mural at 160-05 Highland Avenue is an origin story. When you look at it, you are seeing ordinary teenagers discovering their extraordinary power. The power to change. Do not waste it.
